statement.text:
Let p be a prime. Let G be a transitive subgroup of the group of finitary
permutations F Sym(Ω) of a set Ω, let N be a normal subgroup of G, and let S be a
transitive Sylow p-subgroup of G.
   (a) Is it true that S ∩ N is a Sylow p-subgroup of N ?
   (b) Is it true that SN/N is a Sylow p-subgroup of G/N ?
   (c) Are any two transitive Sylow p-subgroups of G locally conjugate in G?
    Two subgroups X, Y of a group G are said to be locally conjugate if there is
a locally inner automorphism φ of G such that X φ = Y . An automorphism φ of
G is said to be locally inner if for every finite subset A ⊆ G there is an element
g = g(A) ∈ G such that aφ = g −1 ag for all a ∈ A.                        A. O. Asar
